observation: workflow status ends with 'Next: agent-loop workflow approve <task> --by <named-actor>' while showing the Contract only as 'revision N (<path>)'. The goal and acceptance criteria were absent from the text view, though the manifest already carried both and --format=json returned them.

evidence.summary: On UI-29 in voku/agent-ui, workflow status --format=json returned contract reference keys including goal and 3 acceptance_criteria, while the text view of the same task at the same moment showed only Contract: candidate revision 2 (<path>) and then Next: workflow approve. The human asked to approve was given the command and not the subject.
contractReference() already writes goal and acceptance_criteria into the manifest, so the fields existed before this change.

renderText() rendered every reference as state plus a one-line detail(), and the contract detail is revisionDetail() - revision plus path - so the richer fields were dropped by the renderer, not missing from the projection.

tests/WorkflowStatusShowsTheDecisionSubjectTest.php, 5 tests, 11 assertions. Mutation: deleting the renderContractSubject call fails 4 of 5; returning early so only the goal prints fails 1. Both guards are load-bearing. composer ci exit 0 at 1185 tests / 7770 assertions with PHPStan clean.

hypothesis: When one projection is rendered through several views, a field can be present in the structured output and silently absent from the human-facing one. The failure is invisible to schema and contract checks because nothing is missing from the data, only from the rendering a person reads.
validated_conclusion: A view that asks a human to decide must show the subject of the decision in that same view. When adding a fact to a projection, check every renderer that claims to present it; a text renderer built as 'state plus a one-line detail per reference' will quietly truncate any richer field added later. Verify the human-readable view against the structured one rather than assuming they agree.
